vector_await_transaction.description: Wait for a submitted transaction to be confirmed on Vector. Polls until it appears on-chain or the timeout elapses.

timeoutSeconds.description: How long to wait before giving up (default: 120)

vector_build_attestation_attest.description: Build an UNSIGNED transaction that issues an attestation about a registered agent (Part 2 Section 4): a claim by an issuer key about the subject, anchored by the SHA-256 digest of a document. It mints the attestation token named from a seed output of your wallet (the identifier is known before you sign) and locks a deposit of at least 5 AP3X; the issuer takes it back by withdrawal. The issuer key always signs. With issuer_did the issuer is a registered agent: its record must be Active and list the issuer key with the assertion purpose. With solicited the subject's controller co-signs. Every answer gives the COSE Sig_structure for its issued_at: to add an envelope signature, the issuer signs those bytes with its Ed25519 key and builds again with the same issued_at and envelope_sig. Types principal_binding (4) and approval (5) need a salted digest: SHA-256(salt ++ document). The salt stays off-chain with the document, so the owner can delete both. Takes no key material.

changeAddress.description: Your wallet address: it pays the fee and any deposit, gives the collateral, and receives the change. Get it from vector_signer_get_address.

subject.description: The DID of the agent that the attestation is about (its record can be live or ended): did:vector:<64 hex> (the bare 64-hex identifier also works)

issuer.description: The issuer key: it signs the attestation and its envelope: an Ed25519 public key, 64 hex characters (vector_signer_get_public_key shows yours)

issuer_did.description: The DID of the issuer, when the issuer is a registered agent (its record must be Active and list the issuer key with the assertion purpose): did:vector:<64 hex> (the bare 64-hex identifier also works)

att_type.description: The type: identity (0), provenance (1), software (2), environment (3), principal_binding (4), approval (5) or other (15). Software and environment need valid_until.

digest.description: The SHA-256 of the document (64 hex). Types principal_binding (4) and approval (5) need a salted digest: SHA-256(salt ++ document). The salt stays off-chain with the document, so the owner can delete both.

format.description: The CoAP Content-Format number of the document, e.g. 50 for application/json (default: unspecified)

profile.description: The hash of the profile or type URI of the document (64 hex)

locator.description: Where the document can be fetched, e.g. an https URL: 1 to 256 bytes of UTF-8 (default: none)

valid_from.description: When the claim starts to hold (default: unspecified); at or before valid_until (POSIX milliseconds)

valid_until.description: When the claim stops holding: at or after issued_at and at most 366 days after it. Required for software and environment (POSIX milliseconds)

solicited.description: true when the subject asked for the attestation: the subject's controller co-signs (default false)

links.description: Up to 4 links to other attestations. To correct an attestation, issue a new one that supersedes it, then revoke the old one.

target.description: The identifier of the other attestation (64 hex)

deposit.description: AP3X that the attestation locks (default 5, the minimum; more when the ledger minimum of the output is higher)

issued_at.description: Fixes issued_at, which is the end of the validity window: a whole second (a multiple of 1000) within the coming hour. Pass the issued_at of an earlier build to add its envelope signature. valid_minutes has no effect then (POSIX milliseconds)

envelope_sig.description: The issuer's Ed25519 signature (64 bytes, 128 hex) over the sig_structure of an earlier build. Needs that build's issued_at; the builder checks the signature

valid_minutes.description: Minutes from now until the transaction expires (default 30, at most 59): every key holder must sign and the transaction must be submitted before then

vector_build_attestation_contest.description: Build an UNSIGNED transaction in which the subject of an attestation publishes its reply (Part 2 Section 4.1): the attestation's contested field points to the reply (a URI and its SHA-256), and a later reply replaces an earlier one. It works on active, revoked and already contested attestations. The subject's controller signs. Takes no key material.

changeAddress.description: Your wallet address: it pays the fee and any deposit, gives the collateral, and receives the change. Get it from vector_signer_get_address.

attestation.description: The attestation: its identifier (the token name, 64 hex) that the attest build returned

uri.description: Where the subject's reply is, e.g. an https URL: 1 to 256 bytes of UTF-8

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the reply (64 hex)

valid_minutes.description: Minutes from now until the transaction expires (default 30, at most 59): every key holder must sign and the transaction must be submitted before then

vector_build_attestation_revoke.description: Build an UNSIGNED transaction that revokes an active attestation (Part 2 Section 4.1): its status becomes revoked at the start of the validity window with the reason code; nothing else changes. The issuer key signs, or for a registered issuer the controller of its record (by). Ninety days later the issuer can withdraw the deposit. Takes no key material.

changeAddress.description: Your wallet address: it pays the fee and any deposit, gives the collateral, and receives the change. Get it from vector_signer_get_address.

attestation.description: The attestation: its identifier (the token name, 64 hex) that the attest build returned

reason.description: The reason code (default 0, unspecified). Common codes: 1 keyCompromise, 3 affiliationChanged, 4 superseded, 5 cessationOfOperation, 9 privilegeWithdrawn. The contract takes any whole number

by.description: Who signs for the issuer of a registered issuer's attestation: 'issuer' (the issuer key, while the issuer record lists it with the assertion purpose) or 'controller' (the controller of the issuer record). Default: the issuer key while it is listed, else the controller. Without an issuer record only the issuer key can sign.

valid_minutes.description: Minutes from now until the transaction expires (default 30, at most 59): every key holder must sign and the transaction must be submitted before then

vector_build_attestation_withdraw.description: Build an UNSIGNED transaction that withdraws an attestation (Part 2 Section 4.1): it burns the attestation token and returns the deposit to your wallet. This is possible 90 days after the revocation, or 90 days after valid_until; before then the tool names the date. The issuer key signs, or for a registered issuer the controller of its record (by). Takes no key material.

changeAddress.description: Your wallet address: it pays the fee and any deposit, gives the collateral, and receives the change. Get it from vector_signer_get_address.

attestation.description: The attestation: its identifier (the token name, 64 hex) that the attest build returned

by.description: Who signs for the issuer of a registered issuer's attestation: 'issuer' (the issuer key, while the issuer record lists it with the assertion purpose) or 'controller' (the controller of the issuer record). Default: the issuer key while it is listed, else the controller. Without an issuer record only the issuer key can sign.

valid_minutes.description: Minutes from now until the transaction expires (default 30, at most 59): every key holder must sign and the transaction must be submitted before then

vector_build_delegation_delegate.description: Build an UNSIGNED transaction that delegates authority to a registered agent (Part 2 Section 5.2): the delegate may act, with its delegate key, for the actions and resources that the patterns cover, inside the period, and within the value limit. The delegator is a principal key (principal_key) or a registered agent (delegator; its controller or a delegation key signs). With parent it is a sub-delegation: the delegator is the parent's delegate agent, the parent's delegate key signs, and everything must be inside the parent. The delegate key also signs, and no other live delegation may use it (fresh keys). Vault payments need the action marketplace.hire.v1, the resource script:<escrow hash> and a value limit. It mints the delegation token named from a seed output of your wallet; the output holds the ledger minimum of AP3X, which undelegate returns. Takes no key material.

changeAddress.description: Your wallet address: it pays the fee and any deposit, gives the collateral, and receives the change. Get it from vector_signer_get_address.

delegate.description: The DID of the delegate agent, which acts under the delegation (its record must be Active): did:vector:<64 hex> (the bare 64-hex identifier also works)

delegate_key.description: The delegate key: a key that the delegate record lists with the delegation purpose and that no other live delegation uses. It signs this transaction and every use: a key hash (56 hex) or an Ed25519 public key (64 hex)

principal_key.description: A principal as the delegator (a key, not a registered agent): it signs. Not with delegator or parent: a key hash (56 hex) or an Ed25519 public key (64 hex)

organisation.description: With principal_key: the DID or domain of the organisation that the principal acts for (never a person), 1 to 64 bytes

delegator.description: The DID of a registered agent as the delegator (its record must be Active). With parent it is the parent's delegate agent and can be left out: did:vector:<64 hex> (the bare 64-hex identifier also works)

delegator_signer.description: With delegator and no parent: who signs for the agent: 'controller' (default) or a key that its record lists with the delegation purpose (key hash or public key)

parent.description: The parent delegation, for a sub-delegation: its identifier (64 hex). The parent's delegate agent is the delegator, and the parent's delegate key signs

actions.description: What the delegate may do: 1 to 16 action patterns: "*", a name such as marketplace.hire.v1, a prefix such as ocr.* (covers ocr.extract, not ocrx), or oauth:, mcp: or https:// with visible characters after it (matched exactly). A sub-delegation's parent must cover each pattern

resources.description: On what: 0 to 8 resource patterns: "*", script:<56 lowercase hex> (a script; vault payments use script:<escrow hash>), or oauth:, mcp: or https:// with visible characters after it. Default none, which covers no resource

not_before.description: When the delegation starts; default the start of the validity window (for a sub-delegation, not before the parent's start) (POSIX milliseconds)

not_after.description: When the delegation ends; a sub-delegation ends at or before its parent (POSIX milliseconds)

remaining.description: How many further levels of sub-delegation this delegation allows (default 0: none); its depth plus remaining is at most 4

purpose.description: The purpose: the 32-byte hash (64 hex) of a purpose text or mandate

value_limit.description: A spending limit; vault payments need one. Under a parent with a limit, the child needs one inside it (per_tx and total at most the parent's, period_ms at least the parent's)

per_tx.description: The most AP3X that one payment may spend

total.description: The most AP3X that the payments of one period may spend together (at most 10,000); at least per_tx

period_ms.description: The length of a period in milliseconds, e.g. 86400000 for one day

valid_minutes.description: Minutes from now until the transaction expires (default 30, at most 59): every key holder must sign and the transaction must be submitted before then

vector_build_delegation_undelegate.description: Build an UNSIGNED transaction that ends a delegation (Part 2 Section 5.2): it burns the delegation token and returns its AP3X to your wallet. Every delegation below it becomes unusable at once. The delegator signs: the delegator of this delegation or of an ancestor (a principal key, or a delegator agent's controller or delegation key). Takes no key material.

changeAddress.description: Your wallet address: it pays the fee and any deposit, gives the collateral, and receives the change. Get it from vector_signer_get_address.

delegation.description: The delegation to end: its identifier (the token name, 64 hex)

signer.description: The key that signs: the delegator's key of this delegation or of an ancestor. Default: this delegation's delegator (its principal key, or its agent's controller): a key hash (56 hex) or an Ed25519 public key (64 hex)

valid_minutes.description: Minutes from now until the transaction expires (default 30, at most 59): every key holder must sign and the transaction must be submitted before then

vector_build_deploy_contract.description: Build an UNSIGNED transaction deploying a Plutus/Aiken smart contract (locks AP3X at its script address). Takes no key material - sign with your local signer, then broadcast with vector_submit_transaction and confirm with vector_await_transaction.

changeAddress.description: Your wallet address (holds the AP3X; receives change). Get it from your local signer's vector_signer_get_address.

scriptCbor.description: Compiled Plutus/Aiken script in CBOR hex format

initialDatum.description: Initial datum as CBOR hex. Use 'd87980' for void/unit datum. Defaults to void if omitted.

lovelaceAmount.description: AP3X to lock at the script address in lovelace (default: 2,000,000 = 2 AP3X)

vector_build_deregister_agent.description: Build an UNSIGNED transaction that deregisters a LEGACY registry record (did:vector:agent:...) that will not adopt into the identity registry: burns its token and returns the deposit to the owner wallet; its DID then resolves as deactivated. To move a legacy record into the identity registry instead, use vector_build_identity_adopt. Takes no key material. Sign locally with vector_signer_sign, broadcast with vector_submit_transaction, then confirm with vector_await_transaction.

changeAddress.description: The legacy record OWNER's wallet address (receives the returned deposit). Get it from vector_signer_get_address.

vector_build_document_publish.description: Build an UNSIGNED transaction that publishes a document on chain (Module-1 jury specification, Section 10). The transaction carries the document as metadata under label 22084, in text chunks of at most 64 bytes. The answer gives the transaction id, the document URI (vector-tx: and the transaction id) and the blake2b-256 hash of the document. Use the URI and the hash in a Module-1 claim or challenge. The URI is valid when the transaction is on chain. Signing does not change the transaction id. Only your wallet key signs. Takes no key material.

changeAddress.description: Your wallet address: it pays the fee and any deposit, gives the collateral, and receives the change. Get it from vector_signer_get_address.

text.description: The document (JSON for the jury documents) as UTF-8 text. Give the text or the base64 form, not both

base64.description: The document as base64 of the exact bytes (the bytes must be UTF-8 text). Use it when the exact bytes matter, for example to keep line ends

type.description: The document type: claim, evidence, juror-prompt, juror-record, resolution, or another short text (at most 64 bytes)

media_type.description: The media type of the document (default application/json)

valid_minutes.description: Minutes from now until the transaction expires (default 30, at most 59): every key holder must sign and the transaction must be submitted before then

vector_build_identity_adopt.description: Build an UNSIGNED transaction that adopts a legacy agent record into the Vector identity registry (did:vector): it deregisters the legacy record, burns its legacy token and mints the identity token of the same identifier, so the agent keeps its identifier. The identifier must be on the adoption allowlist: pass `proof`, or the server computes it from the published allowlist. Each legacy profile field that fits the identity limits is copied; give a new value for each field that does not (a refusal lists them). The transaction also pays 10 AP3X to the legacy owner key, as the legacy deregistration requires (back to your wallet when your wallet is the owner). The legacy owner key, the controller, each listed Ed25519 key and each key-hash party sign; Module-1 as a party consents through its withdrawal. Takes no key material.

changeAddress.description: Your wallet address: it pays the fee and any deposit, gives the collateral, and receives the change. Get it from vector_signer_get_address.

did.description: The DID of the legacy agent to adopt (did:vector:agent:<legacy policy>:<64 hex> or did:vector:<64 hex>): did:vector:<64 hex> (the bare 64-hex identifier also works)

controller.description: The controller key of the adopted record: an Ed25519 public key, 64 hex characters (vector_signer_get_public_key shows yours)

keys.description: Listed keys (up to 8): the keys that act for the agent. Each new Ed25519 key signs the adoption.

key.description: The public key: 64 hex characters for Ed25519, 66 for a compressed P-256 point

purposes.description: What the key may do: authentication, assertion, transaction, delegation (a P-256 key: authentication and assertion only)

pop.description: P-256 only: the 64-byte ES256 signature by this key over "did:vector:<id>#<key hash>" (r || s, hex)

parties.description: Parties (up to 8). A record needs at least one Accountable Party that covers the validity window (for example { role: "Accountable", signer: "controller" }).

role.description: Accountable, Responsible, Provider, Distributor or Guardian

signer.description: Who signs for the party: 'controller' (whoever is the record's controller), 'module1' (the approved dispute contract; Accountable or Responsible only), or a key hash (56 hex characters)

organisation.description: The DID or domain of an organisation that the party acts for (never a person), 1 to 64 bytes

not_before.description: When the party starts to count; default the start of the validity window (POSIX milliseconds)

not_after.description: When the party stops counting; default never (POSIX milliseconds)

rights.description: The party's rights: suspend, revoke, recover. Default: the highest rights of the role (Accountable suspend+revoke, Responsible and Provider suspend, Distributor none, Guardian recover)

guardian_threshold.description: How many guardians must act together to replace a lost controller key (default 0: no recovery); at most the number of Guardian parties with the recover right

name.description: New agent name, 1 to 64 bytes; default the legacy name when it fits

description.description: New description, up to 256 bytes; default the legacy description when it fits

framework.description: New framework, up to 64 bytes; default the legacy framework when it fits

endpoint.description: New endpoint URL, up to 256 bytes; default the legacy endpoint when it fits

capabilities.description: New capability ids, up to 16 of 1 to 64 bytes, no duplicates; default the legacy list when it fits

proof.description: The Merkle proof of the identifier on the adoption allowlist: the 32-byte nodes (64 hex characters each) from the leaf upward. Default: computed from the allowlist that the deployment publishes

deposit.description: AP3X that the new record locks (default 10, the minimum; a large record needs its ledger minimum, which the builder takes when it is higher)

valid_minutes.description: Minutes from now until the transaction expires (default 30, at most 59): every key holder must sign and the transaction must be submitted before then

vector_build_identity_change_controller.description: Build an UNSIGNED transaction that installs a new controller key on a live did:vector record. It ends every subagent of the agent (the subagent epoch rises by one) and cancels a pending recovery; holds stay. The old and the new controller keys sign. Takes no key material.

changeAddress.description: Your wallet address: it pays the fee and any deposit, gives the collateral, and receives the change. Get it from vector_signer_get_address.

did.description: The DID of the agent whose controller changes: did:vector:<64 hex> (the bare 64-hex identifier also works)

new_controller.description: The new controller key: an Ed25519 public key, 64 hex characters (vector_signer_get_public_key shows yours)

valid_minutes.description: Minutes from now until the transaction expires (default 30, at most 59): every key holder must sign and the transaction must be submitted before then

vector_build_identity_end_subagents.description: Build an UNSIGNED transaction that ends every subagent of an agent at once: it raises the record's subagent epoch by one, and each subagent created under an older epoch resolves as revoked (parentRevoked). The controller signs. Takes no key material.

did.description: The DID of the agent whose subagents end: did:vector:<64 hex> (the bare 64-hex identifier also works)

valid_minutes.description: Minutes from now until the transaction expires (default 30, at most 59): every key holder must sign and the transaction must be submitted before then

vector_build_identity_reclaim.description: Build an UNSIGNED transaction that takes back the AP3X of an ended (Revoked or Retired) did:vector record above the ledger minimum. The tombstone stays unchanged with the ledger minimum; the rest returns to the wallet. The controller signs. Takes no key material.

changeAddress.description: Your wallet address: it pays the fee and any deposit, gives the collateral, and receives the change. Get it from vector_signer_get_address.

did.description: The DID of the ended agent: did:vector:<64 hex> (the bare 64-hex identifier also works)

valid_minutes.description: Minutes from now until the transaction expires (default 30, at most 59): every key holder must sign and the transaction must be submitted before then

vector_build_identity_recovery_cancel.description: Build an UNSIGNED transaction that cancels the pending recovery of a live did:vector record: enough guardians (at least the guardian threshold) sign. Takes no key material.

changeAddress.description: Your wallet address: it pays the fee and any deposit, gives the collateral, and receives the change. Get it from vector_signer_get_address.

did.description: The DID of the agent whose recovery ends: did:vector:<64 hex> (the bare 64-hex identifier also works)

guardians.description: The guardians that act, each by its key hash (56 hex characters) or by its position in the party list (from 0): at least the guardian threshold of them. Each one signs

anyOf.description: A guardian: a key hash, 56 hex characters

vector_build_identity_recovery_complete.description: Build an UNSIGNED transaction that completes the pending recovery of a live did:vector record once its 7 days have passed: the new controller key takes over, and every subagent ends (the subagent epoch rises by one). Anybody can submit it: only the wallet signs. Takes no key material.

Anybody can complete the recovery 7 days later with vector_build_identity_recovery_complete; until then the guardians can cancel it. Takes no key material.

did.description: The DID of the agent to recover: did:vector:<64 hex> (the bare 64-hex identifier also works)

guardians.description: The guardians that act, each by its key hash (56 hex characters) or by its position in the party list (from 0): at least the guardian threshold of them. Each one signs

vector_build_identity_register.description: Build an UNSIGNED transaction that registers a new agent in the Vector identity registry (did:vector): it mints the identity token named from a seed output of your wallet, so the DID is known before you sign, and locks a deposit of at least 10 AP3X in the record. The record names a controller key (the only key that can change it), listed keys with their purposes, and parties; at least one Accountable Party must cover the validity window. With `parent` it registers a subagent of that agent (no endpoint; the parent controller signs too). The controller, each listed Ed25519 key, each key-hash party and a parent controller must sign; Module-1 as a party consents through its withdrawal. Takes no key material.

changeAddress.description: Your wallet address: it pays the fee and any deposit, gives the collateral, and receives the change. Get it from vector_signer_get_address.

name.description: Agent name, 1 to 64 bytes of UTF-8

endpoint.description: Endpoint URL, up to 256 bytes (a subagent has none)

capabilities.description: Capability ids, up to 16 of 1 to 64 bytes, no duplicates

keys.description: Listed keys (up to 8): the keys that act for the agent. Each new Ed25519 key signs the registration.

key.description: The public key: 64 hex characters for Ed25519, 66 for a compressed P-256 point

purposes.description: What the key may do: authentication, assertion, transaction, delegation (a P-256 key: authentication and assertion only)

pop.description: P-256 only: the 64-byte ES256 signature by this key over "did:vector:<id>#<key hash>" (r || s, hex)

parties.description: Parties (up to 8). A record needs at least one Accountable Party that covers the validity window (for example { role: "Accountable", signer: "controller" }).

role.description: Accountable, Responsible, Provider, Distributor or Guardian

signer.description: Who signs for the party: 'controller' (whoever is the record's controller), 'module1' (the approved dispute contract; Accountable or Responsible only), or a key hash (56 hex characters)

organisation.description: The DID or domain of an organisation that the party acts for (never a person), 1 to 64 bytes

vector_build_identity_retire.description: Build an UNSIGNED transaction that retires a live did:vector record for good: the record becomes a tombstone with status Retired. The controller signs, and so does the controller of a successor. By default the tombstone keeps its AP3X; with take_deposit it keeps only the ledger minimum and the rest returns to the wallet. Takes no key material.

did.description: The DID of the agent to retire: did:vector:<64 hex> (the bare 64-hex identifier also works)

successor.description: The DID of the successor: another live, independent agent whose controller signs too: did:vector:<64 hex> (the bare 64-hex identifier also works)

vector_build_identity_revoke.description: Build an UNSIGNED transaction that revokes a live did:vector record for good: the record becomes a tombstone (keys, parties, holds and most profile fields are cleared; the identifier, controller and name stay). The controller or a party with the revoke right acts and signs. The reason code is public for ever. invalid_from makes signatures by the record's keys from that time on invalid (a keyCompromise needs it). Only the controller names a successor, whose controller signs too. Takes no key material.

did.description: The DID of the agent to revoke: did:vector:<64 hex> (the bare 64-hex identifier also works)

party_index.description: The party's position in the record's party list, from 0

role.description: Accountable, Responsible, Provider, Distributor or Guardian

signer.description: Who signs for the party: 'controller' (whoever is the record's controller), 'module1' (the approved dispute contract; Accountable or Responsible only), or a key hash (56 hex characters)

vector_build_identity_set_successor.description: Build an UNSIGNED transaction that names the successor of an ended (Revoked or Retired) did:vector record that has none yet, also after a party revoked it. The successor is another live, independent agent. The controller of the ended record and the controller of the successor sign. Takes no key material.

vector_build_marketplace_reclaim.description: Build an UNSIGNED transaction that reclaims your escrow after deliver_by when the supplier never submitted (state Open or Claimed): everything returns to you. An identity-marketplace escrow with a refund address (every one that vector_build_marketplace_post_escrow posts in that layout) can be reclaimed by anybody: the caller's wallet pays the fee, and everything the escrow holds goes to the refund address. Everything the escrow holds goes to its refund address, or to the buyer key's enterprise address when it names none. Your wallet only pays the fee. Takes no key material.

vector_build_module1_challenge.description: Build an UNSIGNED Module-1 OpenChallenge transaction (oracle mode). It spends the claim (MarkChallenged: the claim state becomes Challenged), mints the challenge token and locks your stake (at least the claim stake) in a new challenge output in state PendingOracle. Your wallet key is the auditor credential: it must be the controller or a listed transaction key of the auditor DID, and the DID must be Active. Give the evidence document as for a claim. The resolution deadline is the time that the oracle has to resolve (default 72 h). The Module-1 jury decides the challenge, and the relay signs its result. The jury needs at least 6 h 10 min: with less time the relay resolves the challenge as Inconclusive at once. Your wallet key signs. Takes no key material.

vector_build_module1_claim.description: Build an UNSIGNED Module-1 SubmitClaim transaction (oracle mode). It mints the claim token and locks your stake (at least 50 AP3X on mainnet) in a new claim output with the claim document hash and URI. Your wallet key is the claimer credential: it must be the controller or a listed transaction key of the claimer DID, and the DID must be Active. Publish the claim document first with vector_build_document_publish. Without claim_hash, the tool reads the document from claim_uri and computes its hash. Anybody can challenge the claim during the challenge window; the Module-1 jury then decides the dispute (vector_get_jury_cases). Your wallet key signs. Takes no key material.

Takes no key material.

vector_marketplace_get_job.description: Poll a marketplace job. Returns pending, failed, or done with the result and the supplier's signed receipt. Template-contract suppliers only in this release. escrow_ref is the one vector_build_marketplace_post_escrow returned and job_id the one vector_marketplace_send_job returned. buyerAddress is required and must be the wallet that posted AND funded the escrow (escrows funded from another key are refused). Works while the escrow is Open, Claimed or Submitted, and after it has been accepted or released. A failed answer can carry the reason malformed_response (the supplier said 200 without a receipt) or escrow_mismatch (its answer was for another escrow). The poll waits up to 20 s. It reads the Post output and asks the supplier, so it cannot show where the escrow stands now or the accept clock: vector_build_marketplace_accept is the way to check (it builds only for a Submitted escrow and prints the seconds left). A job id is a bearer token for its result: pass it only with the escrow it came from. This tool trusts the buyer address and escrow ref your assistant passes; keep its tool use scoped to escrows you posted. A client-side binding to your signer key is planned.

The sha256 of the manifest's bytes is held against the advert's detail hash and reported as a match or a mismatch; a manifest that could not be fetched is reported as such and is never a match. vector_marketplace_list_capabilities.description: List the capability ids currently advertised on the Vector agents marketplace, with supplier counts. Read-only.

vector_marketplace_list_suppliers.description: List supplier adverts on the Vector agents marketplace (advert ref, agent DID, model, price, bonds, processing window, status). Read-only. Pick an advert_ref here, then hire it with vector_build_marketplace_post_escrow. An identity-marketplace advert names its agent (did:vector:<id>); a legacy advert has none ('-'). Fleet adverts (llm.text.generate.*, llm.chat.*, ocr.page.extract.*, audio.synthesize.*) are marked 'not hireable through these tools (fleet route)': post_escrow refuses them.

only_free.description: Only suppliers currently reporting status 'free' (default true)

vector_marketplace_send_job.description: Send the job payload to the supplier of a posted escrow and get back a job id. Call it once the post is confirmed (vector_await_transaction). Template-contract suppliers only in this release. escrow_ref is the one vector_build_marketplace_post_escrow returned. buyerAddress is required and must be the wallet that posted AND funded the escrow (escrows funded from another key are refused). payload must be byte-identical to the one given at post time. The payload goes to the endpoint named by the escrow's advert, and the whole call, checks included, waits up to 90 s for the supplier to answer. Then poll with vector_marketplace_get_job. This tool trusts the buyer address and escrow ref your assistant passes; keep its tool use scoped to escrows you posted. A client-side binding to your signer key is planned.

escrow_ref.description: The escrow_ref that vector_build_marketplace_post_escrow returned, once its transaction is confirmed

payload.description: The same payload string you gave vector_build_marketplace_post_escrow, byte for byte

buyerAddress.description: The wallet address that posted AND funded the escrow (vector_signer_get_address). Escrows funded from another key are refused

vector_marketplace_verify_receipt.description: Check a template-contract supplier's receipt without trusting the supplier. Six checks, each reported pass, FAIL or skipped: (1) receipt.escrow_ref equals the escrow ref; (2) sha256 of the result text equals the receipt's response_hash; (3) the supplier's public key hashes to receipt.supplier_pkh and to the escrow's supplier_pkh; (4) the Ed25519 signature over the canonical receipt verifies; (5) the escrow's result_receipt_hash on chain equals the hash of the signed receipt; (6) the receipt has exactly the fields of its escrow's layout: the 8 receipt fields for a legacy escrow, and those 8 plus agent_did = did:vector:<agent_id> for an identity-marketplace escrow. One extra row, not one of the six: the receipt's prompt_hash equals the escrow's prompt_hash. Says verified only when every row passes. Pass the result text exactly as vector_marketplace_get_job returned it (from its JSON block, not the shortened view), or check 2 is skipped. Works before and after the Accept: check 5 finds the escrow's Submitted output on chain, live or, once it is spent, through the marketplace indexer (which only says where to look: the output is read from Koios and proven to be the escrow's own by the spend chain); pass submitted_ref to name it yourself. Read-only; the supplier's key is read from its /capability unless you pass supplier_pub_key_hex.

receipt.description: The receipt object (or its JSON text) exactly as vector_marketplace_get_job returned it

receipt_signature.description: The hex Ed25519 signature exactly as vector_marketplace_get_job returned it

result.description: The full result text exactly as vector_marketplace_get_job returned it (the JSON block, not the shortened view). Without it check 2 is skipped

supplier_pub_key_hex.description: The supplier's public key, 64 hex characters. Normally read from the supplier's /capability; it has to hash to the escrow's supplier_pkh either way

submitted_ref.description: Optional: the escrow's Submitted output, '<txid>#<index>', to skip the lookup. It is read from Koios and checked against the escrow exactly like one that is looked up

vector_resolve_did.description: Resolve a did:vector DID through the identity gateway (DID Resolution v1.0: GET /1.0/identifiers/{did}). Accepts the canonical form did:vector:<64 hex> and the legacy form did:vector:agent:<policyId>:<64 hex>. Returns the HTTP status and the DID resolution result unchanged: the DID document and its metadata (effective status, keys, parties, profile, record output). Optional versionId or versionTime resolve an earlier version. Read-only, no wallet needed.

did.description: The DID to resolve: did:vector:<64 hex> (canonical) or did:vector:agent:<policyId>:<nftAssetName> (legacy)

versionId.description: Resolve this version: '0', or a decimal number without leading zeros. Do not combine with versionTime.

versionTime.description: Resolve the DID as it was at this time: YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ (UTC, whole seconds). Do not combine with versionId.

vector_self_improvement_analyze_metrics.description: Analyze proposal metrics of the Module-6 (self-improvement) module: proposal activity, adoption rate, treasury health, and engagement statistics. Read-only, takes no key material.

deployment.description: Which Module-6 deployment to read: 'current' (default; the deployment on the identity registry that this server is configured for) or 'previous' (the deployment before the identity registry; its positions stay there until their owners exit)

vector_self_improvement_browse.description: Browse improvement proposals, critiques, endorsements and the treasury of the Module-6 (self-improvement) module: reads the outputs at the module's script addresses and decodes their datums. The current deployment lists created positions only (each holds its token). Read-only.

state.description: Filter proposals by state: Open, Amended, Adopted, Rejected, Expired, Withdrawn

proposalType.description: Filter proposals by type: ParameterChange, TreasurySpend, ProtocolUpgrade, GameActivation, GeneralSuggestion

proposerDid.description: Filter proposals by proposer: did:vector:<64 hex> (the legacy form and the bare 64-hex identifier also work)

proposalTxHash.description: Filter critiques/endorsements by their proposal: the transaction hash of the proposal's seed (the lock that its submission spent) or of its current output

deployment.description: Which Module-6 deployment to read: 'current' (default; the deployment on the identity registry that this server is configured for) or 'previous' (the deployment before the identity registry; its positions stay there until their owners exit)

vector_submit_transaction.description: Submit an already-signed transaction to Vector. Use this to broadcast CBOR signed elsewhere (for example by a local signer). Does not sign anything.

signedTxCbor.description: Hex-encoded CBOR of a fully signed transaction
